title: module.name
goal: By the end of this lesson you will know how to call a tool with module.name after you import the module.
idea: After import math you reach a tool with a dot, like math.sqrt(16) or math.pi. The pattern is always module.name. The module owns the tool and the dot picks which one you want.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change math.sqrt(16) to math.sqrt(36) and press Run. The first line should be 6.0.

practice.text: Import math. Print the square root of 81.
practice.hint: After import math, use the dot pattern with math.sqrt(...) inside print(). The number inside sqrt should be 81.
practice.starterTip: Try print(math.sqrt(81)). You should see 9.0 when you Run.

practice.text: Import math. Print floor of 9.8 and ceil of 9.1.
practice.hint: Use math.floor(9.8) on one print line and math.ceil(9.1) on the other. floor rounds down and ceil rounds up.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 9 and 10 print via floor/ceil.

quiz.question: How do you call sqrt after import math?
quiz.wrong: Put a dot after the module.

quiz.question: What does the dot mean?

options.text: Pick a name inside the module

quiz.correct: Yes, the dot reaches into the toolbox.

quiz.question: Is math.pi a function call?

options.text: No. It is a value you can print

quiz.correct: Right, pi is just a value you can print.
quiz.wrong: Functions need parentheses, and pi has none.

project.title: Dot Practice
project.desc: Import math. Print the sqrt of 49, the floor of 4.2, and pi rounded with round(math.pi, 2).
